# Health

## Scope

Applies when the change touches clinical or patient data, medical devices, GxP systems. Not when the product holds no health data, is no medical device, and keeps no GxP record. Neighbours: `aidd-team:privacy-by-default`, `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`, `aidd-team:incident-response`.

## Terms

- **PHI**: Health information that identifies a person, held by a covered entity or its business associate (US, HIPAA).
- **Covered entity and business associate**: The provider or plan, and the vendor that handles PHI for it under a business associate agreement (US, HIPAA).
- **Minimum necessary**: Use and disclose only the PHI the purpose needs (US, HIPAA).
- **Resource and profile**: A FHIR resource is the base type (Patient); a profile such as US Core constrains it.
- **Information blocking**: A practice that interferes with access to electronic health information, unless an exception applies (US, ONC).

## Invariants and missed cases

| Always true | The case a plan misses |
| --- | --- |
| Every access to PHI is logged: who, what, and why. | A batch export, a support user's impersonation, or a cached report. |
| A patient's access to their own records is never blocked or slowed. | A rate limit or a manual review on the patient-facing API. |
| Clinical data is amended, never silently changed. | Merging duplicate patient records without the history of each. |
| A value keeps its unit and its code (UCUM, LOINC, SNOMED CT). | A dose or a lab result stored as a bare number. |

## Checklist by loop step

| Step | Item | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Clinical or patient data is privacy and compliance: major, the privacy and compliance pools, a DPIA or HIPAA risk analysis. GxP software: references/life-sciences.md. | S1 |
| Before the first edit (`aidd gate --paths`) | Name whether the software is a medical device by its intended use (FDA's CDS and general wellness guidances in the US; MDR Rule 11 and MDCG 2019-11 in the EU), and its class. | S9, S8 |
| Specify | Minimum necessary data and access logging. The FHIR resources, US Core profiles, and SMART scopes each client gets. Device software's safety class (IEC 62304). | S1, S2, S3, S7 |
| Specify | A certified API or a patient's access request is never blocked or slowed without an information blocking exception, recorded (45 CFR Part 171). | S4 |
| Implement | PHI encrypted in transit and at rest; an audit log for every access; no PHI in logs, fixtures, or prompts. A US health app outside HIPAA reports a breach under the FTC rule. | S1 |
| Implement | Device software: the IEC 81001-5-1 activities (threat model, secure coding, security tests). For a cyber device, also an SBOM per release and a vulnerability monitoring and disclosure plan (524B). | S6, S5 |
| Implement | EU: an EHR system, or a wellness app claiming to work with one, meets the EHDS requirements, logging included. | S9 |
| Review | The hazard analysis (ISO 14971) is updated for the change; requirements trace to tests. | S7 |
| Review | Assurance follows the intended use's risk (CSA): scripted tests where a failure harms quality or safety, unscripted ones elsewhere; device software's records meet the QMSR. | S8 |
| Review | Patient-facing pages and apps meet WCAG 2.1 AA where Section 504 or the ADA reaches (US), and the EAA's standard in the EU. | S10 |
| Roll out | Access-log anomalies and errors on clinical paths are rollback triggers; the incident reporting path is known. | S1 |

## Test commands

| Command | Proves | How | Standard |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FHIR validation | every produced resource validates against its profile | the HL7 FHIR validator (`validator_cli.jar`, 6.10.4) | S2 |
| SMART scope tests | a token without a scope reads nothing that scope guards, and each US Core read returns only its profile's data | integration tests per scope and per profile against a test FHIR server | S3 |
| PHI scan | no PHI in logs, fixtures, or outputs | Presidio (`presidio-analyzer` 2.2.364) or another scanner | S1 |
| Access-control tests | each role sees only its records | tests per role and per record | S1 |
| Traceability check | every requirement has a test | requirements and their tests linked in StrictDoc (`uvx strictdoc==0.30.1 export .`, failing on a link to a missing node), and a check that each requirement links a test | S7 |

- From `aidd-team:enterprise-controls`: Dependency scan, Container scan and SBOM.
- From `aidd-team:threat-model`: Abuse-case tests.
- From `aidd-team:accessible-ui`: Accessibility per state.

## Keep it current

Each entry is due after its `review_every_days` (else emerging 90 days, established 365) or by its `review_due`. An emerging one applies only when the change needs it, said in the Spec. One `aidd eval standards` lists as due is looked up in Specify, and a missing one is proposed to aidd's `schemas/industry-standards.json`.
